chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibrahim al-Kharqiyy, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Whoever walks to fulfill the need of his believing brother, seeking thereby what is with Allah, until it is fulfilled for him, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will write for him the like of the reward of a Hajj and an Umrah, both accepted, and the fasting of two months from the Sacred months, and their I'tikaf in the Sacred Mosque.'
And whoever walks for it with intention but it is not fulfilled, Allah will write for him the like of an accepted Hajj. Therefore, desire the good.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for helping a Muslim brother in need according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to emphasize the social dimension of worship, where physical effort in serving a believer is elevated to the status of major acts of devotion like Hajj and I'tikaf. The hadith uniquely distinguishes between the reward for successful fulfillment and the reward for sincere intention even if the task remains incomplete, encouraging persistent effort in communal solidarity. This reflects the Shia emphasis on 'ta'awun' (cooperation) as a tangible expression of faith.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibrahim Al Kharqy who said,

‘I heard Abu Abdullahasws saying: ‘The one who walks regarding a need of his Momin brother, seeking by that what is in the Presence of Allahazwj, until he fulfils it for him, Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic would Write for him due to that, the like of the Recompense of a Hajj and an Umrah, both having performed correctly, and Fasts of two months from the Sacred months, and both during Itikaaf in the Sacred Masjid;

and the one who walks regarding it with an intention but could not fulfil it, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Write for him, due to that, like of a correctly performed Hajj. Therefore, be desiring regarding the goodness’.
en.sarwar: 9. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from ibn Mahbub from Ibrahim al-Khariqi who has said the following:

“I heard abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) saying, ‘Whoever walks to help make the wish of his believing brother (in belief) come true, seeking thereby the reward for it with Allah until he makes it happen, Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, writes down for him a reward equal to the reward for performing Hajj and ‘Umrah that are of virtuous deeds, fasting for two of the sacred months while spending this time in the Sacred Mosque performing ‘I’tikaf (a certain form of worship),
and if one walks with the intention to help, but does not make it come true, Allah still writes down for him the reward for one Hajj that is accepted. Therefore, be interested in good deeds.’”
